title: Panel vote notes + role scorecard draft (Runtime Engineering)
content:
Quick context:
- Role: Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime (inference backend team)
- Candidate: external referral (via Sofia)
- Interview date: 2026-03-11 
- Rounds: System design (Katherine), Coding (Dev), Culture/ownership + perf tradeoffs (Sofia), Hiring manager sync (Liam)

High-level impression (notes to self):
- Strong systems intuition, clear tradeoff articulation for latency vs cost.
- Hands-on with GPU inference stacks? Candidate has used Triton and ONNX runtime but mostly from application side; some gaps on kernel-level optimizations (CUDA / custom kernels).
- Good at designing for observability and failure modes — proposed sensible tracing points and fallback flow.
- Communication: concise, asks clarifying Qs without stalling.
- Culture fit: pragmatic, leans toward delivery and iteration rather than research-first.

Concrete takeaways by panelist:
- Katherine (system design): liked the fallback routing design (multi-model tiering, async queueing). Wanted more on KV-cache invalidation semantics under model versioning — candidate sketched a solution but not fully confident.
- Dev (coding): completed the exercise (streaming prefix-merging) with reasonable correctness; missed an edge-case around concurrent KV writes but quickly proposed locking/compare-and-swap when prompted. Implementation style neat but lacked micro-optimizations for hot loops.
- Sofia (perf/ops): strong on batching strategies and cache warm-up. Less familiarity with quantized int8 performance regressions; candidate expects upstream libs to handle most.
- Liam (hiring manager): liked ownership instincts, wants someone who can be an early mentor in the team. Concern: candidate hasn't shipped a large-scale inference service from 0 -> prod alone.

Scorecard (draft; 1–5, 5=excellent):
- System design (scale, reliability): 4
- Low-level performance (profiling, CUDA/ops): 3
- Production experience (deploys, rollouts): 3
- Coding ability (correctness & clarity): 4
- Ownership & communication: 5
- Team fit / collaboration: 4
- Security/compliance awareness: 3
- Overall recommended score (weighted): 3.8

Weighting notes: give more weight to system design and ownership (x1.2), lower weight to pure CUDA kernel mastery (x0.8) because team has specialists for kernel work.

Red flags / open questions:
- Hasn’t led a full private/VPC on-prem inference deployment — important for some enterprise customers. Need to verify the depth of experience.
- Quantization experience seems surface-level; will need ramp time for Optimize team's recommendations.
- Salary / compensation: asked about bands, indicated expectation aligned with senior SDE (current comp range unknown). Ask recruiter for current comp before moving to final offer.

Suggested next steps (vote-oriented):
- Panel vote: Proceed to reference check + one-week take-home micro-project OR pass to hiring manager for final onsite depending on consensus. My leaning: move forward to references and a lightweight take-home (2–4 hours) focused on KV-cache eviction & versioning under model rollouts.
- Add to hiring sync: confirm comp band and potential for mentorship responsibilities.
- Reference check to validate: led infra projects, ownership claims, and soft skills under pressure.

Draft feedback blurb for candidate (friendly, concise):
"Really enjoyed our conversations — particularly your pragmatic design for routing and fallbacks. We have a couple logistical follow-ups (references and a brief take-home focused on cache/versioning semantics). We'll circle back with next steps in the next 3 business days. — Marcus on behalf of the interview panel"

Notes for take-home exercise (if we do it):
- Goal: validate candidate's thinking on model versioning + KV cache correctness under concurrent traffic and rollouts.
- Constraints: 2–4 hours, pseudo-code + small test harness (Python or Go), explain tradeoffs and failure modes.
- Evaluation rubric: correctness (40%), reasoning & tradeoffs (40%), clarity & tests (20%).

Follow-ups for hiring flow:
- Recruiter (Emma Tran) to collect comp info and schedule reference call.
- Engineering lead (Liam) to decide on take-home vs direct reference route.
- If moving to offer, include 30/60/90 goals: onboarding debug flow, one rollout owner, mentor 1 junior.

Random notes / fragments I want to keep:
- Candidate mentioned a past project: "Adaptive KV coalescing" — ask for code link. Might be a good signal of product-level thinking. (PR/commit link request)
- Check PR above (linked_artifacts) for similar naming conventions.
- Could be fast ramp to a Staff-1 track with strong coaching; potential hiring upside if we pair with Optimize team for quantization ramp.

Personal vote (Marcus): Proceed to references + take-home. If references strong, hire at Senior SDE band with clear growth plan into Runtime lead areas.

Unresolved items to capture before final panel vote:
- Exact current comp (from recruiter)
- One specific example of a production outage they debugged end-to-end (we want timeline + root cause)
- Link to any public code or internal PRs they can share

End of notes.

(Will iterate this into a final panel summary if panel agrees on next steps.)
